lede: A rainforest-covered sand cay inside the Great Barrier Reef World Heritage Area, and the only one of about 300 reef cays with rainforest.

walks.name: The Boardwalk
walks.notes: Easy, Grade 1. Wheelchair accessible with assistance. Allow longer to read the signs.

walks.name: Beach walk
walks.notes: Easy. Not wheelchair accessible. Do not attempt at high tide.

timeline.event: Wunyami, "place of spirits", a special place for the Gunggandji people
Captain Cook names the island after astronomer Charles Green
Pleasure cruises begin on the coaster Zeus
Hayles start a regular passenger service from Cairns
World’s first glass-bottom boat; national park declared
Crocodile farm opens, renamed Marineland Melanesia in 1972
Surrounding waters become a marine national park

safety: Marine stingers (jellyfish) may be present at any time, more often in warmer months. Wear a stinger suit to swim or snorkel.
Swim and snorkel between the red and yellow flags on the northern beach, always with a buddy.
Snorkel at high tide, when it is easier to get in and out of the water.
Never stand on coral. Use rest stations or rest on sand.
Wear a hat and sunscreen, and drink plenty of water. Treated water is on tap in the day-use amenities.
The boardwalk can be slippery when wet.
No-take zone: never touch, pick up or take plants or animals. Rangers issue fines.
Don’t feed wildlife, including birds and fish. No drones on the island or over the reef.
Stay on boardwalks and marked tracks.
getting_there: Ferries leave the Reef Fleet Terminal on Spence Street, Cairns, and take 50 to 60 minutes. Helicopter and seaplane services also fly to the island. Toilets, showers, lockers and food are in the resort. A ranger is based on the island; the information counter is in the resort.
